title: Human-in-the-loop approvals: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Privilege gateway
steps.what: Policy hold: a Cedar policy can hold a tool call for a human instead of refusing it, and the hold is written to the gateway log.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.

steps.title: Privilege console
steps.what: The named approver opens Access Request Approvals, then HITL Requests, finds the request under Awaiting, and approves or denies it.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.

steps.title: Approval request API
steps.what: Demo approval path: an approval request is created through the Privilege API (type App, an MCP action on an application, approvers set, one hour expiry) and its status moves from New to Pending.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.

steps.title: Agent key
steps.what: No connection is held open, because an approval takes minutes to hours: the request is refused with a reason, a reference and an expiry, an approver signs, and the agent retries and proceeds.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.

steps.title: Audit log
steps.what: Audit log is one of the components this feature uses.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.

steps.title: Attended and unattended evaluation
steps.what: Policy is asked two questions about every request: may this proceed attended, and may it proceed unattended.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.

steps.title: Single-use bound approval
steps.what: An approval is single-use and bound to the exact call, or to an action for a fixed period, with a configurable number of approvers, named roles and a minimum authentication strength, so one approval cannot be replayed for a second transaction.
steps.why: Some agent actions are too high-risk to let an agent finish alone.
